prompt: Produce exactly one concise sentence as the image caption and nothing else. The sentence must contain 2–6 discrete, visually verifiable facts only, presented in this priority order when present: (1) legible text, (2) counts and canonical object types, (3) color/material/garment modifiers tied to those nouns, (4) pose/action/orientation if visibly discriminative, (5) a simple placement tag (foreground / midground / background) for each non-text fact, (6) lighting or viewpoint only if distinctive. If any legible text appears, transcribe it exactly in double quotes and immediately follow the quotes with a location phrase using on/in/above + the named object (e.g., "Sign reads "London 2012" on the black tablecloth"). If text is not clearly legible, omit it. Use numerals for counts, prefer precise nouns (ladder, food cart, tablecloth, poster, newspaper, bicycle, child, man, woman), place color/material modifiers directly after the noun ("orange ladder", "navy sweater with white collar"), and include a short verb phrase for visible actions ("holding", "leaning", "suspended mid‑air") only when distinctive. For each non‑text fact include a placement tag (e.g., "foreground: orange ladder"). Do not infer roles, intentions, emotions, or functions (do not write "staff", "vendor", "selling", "happy") unless a visible label explicitly shows that word. Do not attribute text to an object unless that object is named; if uncertain which object contains the text, omit the transcription. Keep phrasing simple (present or present‑progressive verbs), separate facts with commas or semicolons, and keep the sentence compact (aim for ≤25 words). Before outputting, ensure the caption is one sentence, contains 2–6 facts, follows the required order and formatting for any included text, and contains no extra commentary.
